detail: Prespecified ACID-family result follows a subgroup and brain-related endpoints. It does not provide a separate raw blueberry or constipation severity trial.
Secondary cardiovascular and inflammatory analysis of the same ACID cohort. No independent constipation endpoint comparison.
Parent ACID trial and its Table 4 report one versus two mild constipation events. This is purified bilberry and black currant, not blueberries.
Protocol mentions potential bowel effects that could unmask treatment. It supplies no observed constipation result.
Secondary history of levodopa. Food examples are citations and not a new Parkinson cohort.
The previously verified independent case describes dyskinesia after fresh sauteed broad beans. No oat exposure.
The original abstract repeats five healthy and six Parkinson participants, the same timing and the same medication comparison as the 1992 study. One probable shared cohort.
The publisher's complete paper separates motor score improvement and severe dyskinesia in three participants after cooked broad beans. Oats were not the intervention.
An odor-identification diagnostic comparison in a cognitively impaired population. It is not the registered training trial's outcome paper.
Protocol names clove as one odor in training and includes Hamilton anxiety. It gives no observed symptom estimate.
